title: Quiet Hours
statement: A team shares one meeting room calendar. Each busy block is [start, end) in minutes and occupies the room from start up to but not including end. Between the earliest start and the latest end, return every gap during which the room is free, as [start, end) blocks sorted by start. Blocks that touch (one ends exactly when another starts) leave no gap.

examples.explanation: The room is busy from 1 to 4 and from 6 to 7, so it is free from 4 to 6.
The blocks touch, so there is no gap.

hints.content: A minute is free if no block covers it.
Sorting the blocks by start lets you sweep left to right.
Track the latest end seen so far.
If the next block starts after that latest end, the room is free in between.
Use 'starts after' (strictly greater), so touching blocks leave no gap, and always extend the latest end with max.

testCases.explanation: The room is busy from 1 to 4 and from 6 to 7, so it is free from 4 to 6.
The blocks touch, so there is no gap.
A single block has no gaps.
Blocks nested inside a long block leave no gaps.
Touching blocks chain together, leaving only [7, 8).

solutions.title: Check every boundary segment
solutions.intuition: Free time can only start or end at block boundaries, so test each segment between consecutive boundaries.
solutions.approach: Collect and sort all distinct starts and ends. For each consecutive pair (x, y), the segment is free if no block covers x. Merge adjacent free segments.
solutions.pseudocode:
points = sorted unique endpoints
for (x, y) consecutive: if no block with s <= x < e: append or extend gap [x, y)
commonMistakes: Using x <= e, which treats the end minute as busy.
solutions.interviewExplanation: Testing each boundary segment against every block is correct, but quadratic.

steps.title: Step 1
steps.content: Points 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 7. Segments starting at 1, 2 and 3 are covered.

steps.title: Step 2
steps.content: The segment [4, 6) is uncovered → gap. [6, 7) is covered.

solutions.title: Sort and sweep the latest end
solutions.intuition: After sorting by start, a gap appears exactly when a block starts after everything before it has ended.
solutions.approach: Sort copies by start. Keep end = the first block's end. For each block, if start > end, record [end, start). Then end = max(end, block end).
commonMistakes: Setting end = e instead of the maximum, which invents gaps after nested blocks.
Using s >= end, which reports zero-length gaps for touching blocks.
solutions.interviewExplanation: Sorting by start and carrying the latest end is the merge-intervals sweep; every time a start jumps past the carried end, that jump is free time. Sorting dominates at O(n log n). For several people's calendars, flatten them first.
